identity.title: PIK-75 suppresses SREBP-dependent sterol-synthesis genes in PIK3CA-altered small-cell lung cancer cells, but attribution to p110alpha remains unresolved.

content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Class IA PI3K isoforms are candidate therapeutic targets in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). The transcriptional consequences of isoform-directed inhibitors in SCLC cells have not been compared genome-wide. METHODS: We re-analysed GEO series GSE40564, in which PIK3CA-altered NCI-H69 cells were treated for 24 h with vehicle, PIK-75 (p110alpha-directed) or TGX-221 (p110beta-directed), with three arrays per group. Differential expression used limma, with re-processing from raw files and spike-in-anchored normalisation as sensitivity analyses. Gene sets were tested with correlation-adjusted competitive tests (camera), including a direct comparison of the two compounds. The main finding was checked against LINCS L1000 signatures of selective PI3K inhibitors and an independent alpelisib RNA-seq dataset. Isoform dependency was examined in DepMap CRISPR screens, and a PIK-75 response score was tested in 81 primary SCLCs against matched random-signature nulls. RESULTS: PIK-75 changed 11,645 of 17,458 genes at FDR < 0.05; 316 decreased and 20 increased significantly beyond two-fold. Its clearest pathway-level effect was lower expression of SREBP-controlled sterol- and lipid-synthesis genes (SQLE, HMGCS1, HMGCR, LDLR, SCD; log2 fold-change -1.1 to -1.6). Cholesterol homeostasis was the only gene set that stayed significant after correlation adjustment (camera FDR = 0.02) and that differed significantly between PIK-75 and TGX-221 (FDR = 0.02). TGX-221 changed 358 genes, none two-fold, and its response depended on two of three replicates. In LINCS, the down-regulated genes of alpelisib and taselisib were enriched for SREBP targets (p  approximately  5 x 10(-)(6)), whereas those of TGX-221 were not, and alpelisib reduced several of the same genes in an independent dataset. PIK-75 also inhibits CDK9 and DNA-PK, and canonical FOXO targets were not induced, so the response cannot be attributed to p110alpha alone. SCLC lines depended more on PIK3CA than on PIK3CB in DepMap (median Chronos -0.38 vs -0.15), as did other lineages. In patients, the response score was not associated with survival beyond matched random signatures (empirical p = 0.12-0.14). CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first genome-wide comparison of isoform-directed PI3K inhibitors in SCLC cells. PIK-75, but not TGX-221, suppresses an SREBP-dependent sterol programme in NCI-H69 cells, and public data from selective p110alpha inhibitors point to PI3K signalling as its most plausible source. Because PIK-75 is not selective and TGX-221 exposure was not measured, the attribution to p110alpha and the apparent dispensability of p110beta remain preliminary.
